workingHypotheses: The strongest master story combines a friendly low-cost-airline personality with the progressive simplification of commercial and booking complexity.

organisingIdea.statement: Make a low-cost airline feel optimistic and easy to explore by sequencing complexity, preserving personality, and simplifying booking decisions without hiding commercial goals.

claims.statement: The project aimed to overhaul an outdated and structurally cluttered airline website and booking experience.
claims.notes: Confirm whether the engagement covered the full site or selected releases.

claims.statement: The work served leisure travellers booking across languages, platforms, and branching itinerary types.
claims.notes: Identify primary markets and accessibility needs.

claims.statement: Alexander describes responsibility for end-to-end UX while working as an Art Director at Dennerlein GmbH.
claims.notes: Confirm the exact title and responsibility during this specific project.

claims.statement: The work took place during Alexander's Dennerlein tenure from October 2014 to August 2017, but exact project dates are not yet known.
claims.notes: Employment window is not a project timeline.

claims.statement: Attributed work includes journey mapping, interaction audits, screen restructuring, booking-flow design, a responsive design system, and a multilingual icon set.
claims.notes: Clarify which pieces were designed personally versus by the visual-design team.

claims.statement: The redesign had to rationalise more than 100 inconsistent pages while supporting accessibility, multiple languages, operational constraints, and complex booking branches.
claims.notes: Confirm the 100+ page count and actual accessibility standard.

claims.statement: Analytics showing missed promotions, low scrolling, and mid-booking drop-off led the team to reprioritise content and place booking functionality first.
claims.notes: Ask which metric or observed behaviour most directly changed a screen.

claims.statement: The booking flow progressively revealed flexible-date, extra, one-way, and return options instead of exposing every branch at once.
claims.notes: Confirm testing evidence and the shipped interaction.

claims.statement: The work was carried out with visual designers, developers, and stakeholders across the business, using mid-fidelity prototypes as a shared decision tool.
claims.notes: Names and specific collaboration moments are missing.

claims.statement: The CV claims the website overhaul contributed to a 15% revenue increase.
claims.notes: Do not publish without a source, measurement window, and credible attribution.

claims.statement: The redesign needed to make a price-led airline feel friendly, optimistic, and useful for discovery without obscuring commercial options.
Related booking decisions were grouped and complexity was introduced progressively instead of splitting every branch across separate screens.
claims.notes: Flight and package selection in one view is a concrete example.

claims.statement: Alexander worked across UX, UI, interaction, booking-flow restructuring, prototyping, motion, photography selection, colour, iconography, illustration direction, and the digital style guide.

claims.statement: A separate 2016 six-week body of work used animated tutorial films and a wider campaign to explain SunExpress online services.
claims.notes: Confirm that this supporting campaign belongs in the public SunExpress master story.

claims.statement: Alexander wrote and art-directed the tutorial film, defined its visual style, designed scenes with a junior illustrator, and worked with a motion designer and voice artist.
claims.notes: Names and exact production credits remain unresolved.

claims.statement: The tutorials combined light-hearted travel stories with step-by-step instruction and modular characters that could support a fast production schedule and wider campaign rollout.
An older portfolio note claims the first tutorial was dubbed into three languages, received more than 50,000 social views, and led to reuse of the character style across further touchpoints.
claims.notes: Do not publish without dated channel evidence or another reliable source.

conflicts.question: The SunExpress factsheet repeats S&P collaborator names; who actually worked on SunExpress?

openQuestions.question: When did the project happen, in what employer or agency context, and for how long?
openQuestions.answer: The relaunch is dated 2017 and seven months; the supporting Tutorials campaign is dated 2016 and six weeks. The work sat within Alexander's Dennerlein GmbH employment.

openQuestions.question: Which booking stages, markets, languages, and platforms were actually in scope?
What did Alexander personally own in the journey, design system, and icon work?
Which parts were implemented, tested, or remained conceptual?
What has visibly aged, what still holds up, and what would Alexander now change?
openQuestions.answer: The visual style has aged more than the information architecture and booking decisions; the exact redesign choices Alexander would make today remain open.

openQuestions.question: Should the 2016 tutorial films and campaign appear as a supporting body of work inside the SunExpress master story?
What did ‘UX was done in a Gunslinger kind of way’ mean in practice, and which decision best captures it?
